baslik: One Thrust Lever Left in Climb on a Wet Runway
sonuc: overran the runway at Congonhas and hit a warehouse
tetik: a thrust lever left in climb position on landing
mekanizma: one engine still producing power so the spoilers never deployed and the jet couldn't stop
ders: Airbus had proposed a warning for this lever error, and the crash renewed attention to it
yanilgi: The runway was slippery, but the key failure was one lever. With it above idle, the spoilers stayed down.
tartisma: The system logic required both levers at idle. Should automation override an obvious landing?
basliklar: Why TAM Flight 3054 Couldn't Stop
The Thrust Lever Left in Climb
hook: One lever was left in climb
sahneler: In rain at São Paulo, an Airbus A320 raced off the end of the runway.
It crossed a road and exploded into a warehouse, killing one hundred ninety nine people.
One thrust reverser had been deactivated.
On touchdown, one thrust lever stayed in climb position.
That engine kept producing power.
The spoilers needed both levers at idle to deploy.
The jet couldn't slow down on the short runway.
Airbus had proposed a warning for this lever error.

baslik: The Locomotives That Ran Past a Stop Signal
sonuc: caused an Amtrak train to hit light locomotives
tetik: a crew failing to stop at signals
mekanizma: locomotives fouling the main line after passing stop signals, with a cab signal whistle taped silent
ders: random drug testing was mandated for safety-sensitive transport jobs
yanilgi: The signals worked. The freight crew didn't stop for them.
tartisma: The crash led to random drug testing across transport. Where should testing stop?
basliklar: Why the Chase, Maryland Train Crash Happened
The Signals the Crew Ignored
sahneler: An Amtrak train at over one hundred miles per hour hit locomotives on its track.
It crashed and killed fourteen passengers and two crew.
Conrail locomotives had run onto the main line.
Their crew failed to stop at the signals.
They tested positive for cannabis.
Their cab warning whistle had been muted with duct tape.
The engineer went to prison.
Congress later mandated random drug testing for safety-sensitive jobs.

baslik: A Ship Knocked Out a Lift Bridge and Cars Fell
sonuc: had spans knocked down by a ship
tetik: a cargo ship striking the low bridge
mekanizma: ship impact on a low vertical-lift bridge with poor navigational clearance
ders: the replacement bridge was built higher with ship-collision islands
yanilgi: It wasn't the first strike. The bridge was hit by ships twice.
tartisma: Clearance problems were known for years. How long should a risky bridge stay in service?
basliklar: Why the Sidney Lanier Bridge Fell
The Bridge Ships Kept Hitting
sahneler: A cargo ship crashed into the Sidney Lanier Bridge in Georgia.
Spans fell into the river, and ten people were killed.
It was a low vertical-lift bridge.
Its navigational clearance was poor.
Cars on the bridge plunged into the water.
It was one of two ship collisions it suffered.
Larger ships later couldn't reach the port at all.
The replacement was built higher, with protective islands.

baslik: The Avalanche That Buried a Town in Minutes
sonuc: triggered an avalanche that buried Yungay
tetik: an earthquake destabilizing Huascarán's north wall
mekanizma: a rock, ice and snow avalanche gathering mud and debris as it raced down the valley
ders: Yungay was declared a national cemetery and the town was rebuilt elsewhere
yanilgi: The earthquake was offshore. The deadliest blow came from a mountain far inland.
tartisma: The disaster came from far outside the shaking zone. How far should hazard maps reach?
basliklar: How the 1970 Peru Earthquake Buried Yungay
The World's Deadliest Avalanche
soru: How far should hazard maps reach?
sahneler: An earthquake struck off the coast of Peru.
Within minutes, a wall of ice and rock buried the town of Yungay.
The shaking broke the north wall of Mount Huascarán.
Ice, rock and snow fell down the valley.
It raced about eighteen kilometres at enormous speed.
It picked up mud and debris as it went.
It became the world's deadliest avalanche.
Yungay's site was declared a national cemetery.

baslik: Half a Mountain Fell on a Highway
tetik: the collapse of Johnson Peak's southwestern slope
mekanizma: a massive rock slope failure, possibly linked to small earthquakes
ders: the new road was built over the debris and the site is a viewpoint
yanilgi: The victims were stopped by a smaller avalanche first. Then the big slide came.
tartisma: A small warning event trapped people in the danger zone. How do you read a warning correctly?
basliklar: What Caused the Hope Slide
Half a Mountain on the Highway
soru: How do you read a warning?
sahneler: In British Columbia, a mountainside collapsed onto a highway.
In seconds, rock buried the road, and four people were killed.
A small avalanche had already stopped cars there.
Two small earthquakes were recorded that morning.
Then Johnson Peak's slope gave way.
Tens of millions of cubic metres of rock came down.
It is one of Canada's largest recorded landslides.
The new highway was built over the debris.

baslik: A Business Jet's Collision Warning Was Switched Off
sonuc: collided mid-air with a business jet over the Amazon
tetik: two jets at the same altitude on opposite headings
mekanizma: controller errors plus a collision-avoidance system that wasn't active on the business jet
ders: Brazil faced scrutiny over its air traffic control system
yanilgi: The business jet survived. Its winglet sliced the airliner's wing off.
tartisma: Brazil's and America's investigators blamed different parties. Who gets the blame when layers fail?
basliklar: Why Gol Flight 1907 Collided Over the Amazon
The Collision Warning That Was Off
sahneler: Over the Amazon, a Boeing 737 and a business jet collided head-on.
The airliner broke up, and all one hundred fifty four aboard were killed.
Both jets were at the same altitude.
Controllers failed to catch it.
The business jet's collision-avoidance system wasn't active.
Its winglet sliced off half of the 737's left wing.
The damaged business jet landed safely.
Investigators disagreed over where blame lay.

baslik: The Jet That Ran Out of Fuel Without Saying Emergency
sonuc: ran out of fuel and crashed on Long Island
tetik: a crew that never declared a fuel emergency
mekanizma: holding delays and a missed approach while controllers didn't understand the fuel state
yanilgi: The crew asked for priority. Controllers didn't treat it as an emergency.
tartisma: One word could have changed the outcome. Should safety depend on the right word?
basliklar: Why Avianca Flight 52 Ran Out of Fuel
The Word the Crew Never Said
soru: Should safety depend on one word?
sahneler: A Boeing 707 ran out of fuel and crashed on a Long Island hillside.
It broke apart, and seventy three people were killed.
The flight was held in three holding patterns.
Fuel ran low.
The crew asked for priority, but never said emergency.
After a missed approach, the engines flamed out.
Controllers didn't grasp how little fuel was left.
Fuel emergency terms were standardized.

baslik: The Rocket That Destroyed Its Own Launch Pad
tetik: engines failing and a pad damaged by the launch
mekanizma: a pad built without flame diverters or water deluge eroded by thrust, while engine failures crippled the vehicle
ders: the pad was rebuilt with protections it had lacked
yanilgi: It was planned as a test. The pad lacked protections most launch sites use.
tartisma: SpaceX called it a learning flight. When is a test failure a success?
basliklar: What Went Wrong on Starship's First Flight
The Launch That Wrecked the Pad
sahneler: The most powerful rocket ever flown lifted off from Texas.
Less than four minutes later, it was destroyed.
Three engines failed to ignite at lift-off.
The blast damaged the launch pad.
Debris spread into a nearby state park.
Multiple engines failed during flight.
SpaceX said it had expected to learn.
The pad had no flame diverters or water deluge system.

baslik: The Bridge Kept Cool With Foil and Air-Conditioning
sonuc: was closed after cracks appeared in its pedestals
mekanizma: cracking in cast-iron pedestals worsening under heat expansion
ders: the bridge needed years of repairs to its bearings and pedestals
yanilgi: The bridge didn't fall. Engineers closed it before it could.
tartisma: Closing a bridge for years costs a community. When is caution too costly?
basliklar: Why Hammersmith Bridge Was Closed
The Bridge Wrapped in Foil
sahneler: Engineers found cracks in the pedestals of London's Hammersmith Bridge.
Suddenly the bridge was closed to all motor traffic.
The pedestals were made of cast iron.
In a heatwave, the cracks worsened.
The bridge was closed to walkers and cyclists too.
Its chains were later wrapped in foil and cooled with air-conditioning.
The goal was to stop further cracking.
Repairs dragged on for years.

baslik: The Ship That Burned at the Dock in Toronto
sonuc: burned at its pier in Toronto Harbour
tetik: a fire in a locked linen closet
mekanizma: a delayed alarm and polished wood paneling letting fire spread through the ship
ders: Canada and the US tightened fire safety rules for passenger ships
yanilgi: The ship was docked, yet at least 118 people died. The fire spread faster than they could escape.
tartisma: A crew member went for keys instead of the alarm. How should crews be trained for fire?
basliklar: Why the SS Noronic Fire Was So Deadly
The Closet Fire That Burned a Ship
sahneler: At night, a passenger ship caught fire while docked in Toronto Harbour.
It spread in minutes, and at least one hundred eighteen people died.
Smoke came from a locked linen closet.
A bellboy ran for the keys without sounding the alarm.
When the closet was opened, fire burst into the hallway.
Polished wood paneling fed the flames.
Most passengers were American tourists.
Fire rules for passenger ships were tightened.

baslik: The Emigrant Ship That Hit a Reef at Full Speed
sonuc: ran aground on a reef off Spain
tetik: a course too close to the coast
mekanizma: grounding at full speed on a reef off Hormigas Island
ders: the wreck deeply affected emigrant communities and scrutiny of ship officers
yanilgi: The reef was known. The ship was simply on a dangerous course.
tartisma: Early reports wrongly accused the captain of fleeing. Why do first reports blame so fast?
basliklar: Why the SS Sirio Was Wrecked
The Emigrant Ship on the Reef
soru: Why do first reports blame so fast?
sahneler: An Italian steamer full of emigrants ran onto a reef off Spain.
It struck at full speed, and at least two hundred people were killed.
It was bound for South America.
Its course ran too close to the coast.
It hit a reef off Hormigas Island.
An eyewitness said it was taking a dangerous course.
Panic broke out, and lifeboats were swamped.
The disaster shook emigrant communities in Italy.

baslik: Seawater in the Batteries, Then Silence
sonuc: vanished and imploded in the South Atlantic
tetik: water leaking through the snorkel into the batteries
mekanizma: a battery fire after seawater entry, followed by loss and implosion
ders: the wreck was found a year later and Argentina's naval readiness came under scrutiny
yanilgi: The crew reported the problem. An implosion was detected within hours.
tartisma: The search took a year. How do you find a submarine that goes silent?
basliklar: What Happened to ARA San Juan
The Submarine That Went Silent
sahneler: An Argentine submarine vanished during a routine patrol.
Within hours, sensors picked up a sound consistent with an implosion.
Its last report described a problem.
Seawater had leaked through the snorkel into the batteries.
It started a fire.
All forty four crew were lost.
The wreck was found a year later at great depth.
Argentina's naval readiness came under scrutiny.
